summary: Vanillaware's Edo-period side-scrolling action RPG, expanded on PlayStation Vita as Muramasa Rebirth.

entries.title: Muramasa: The Demon Blade
entries.definitive_edition: Muramasa Rebirth with Genroku Legends DLC

emulation.emulator: Vita3K as a testing fallback; Dolphin for Wii comparison
emulation.notes: Prefer real Vita/PlayStation TV if compatibility or DLC handling is uncertain.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Complete Vita Rebirth route; Wii/Dolphin has higher raw upscaling but less content.

primary.version: Muramasa Rebirth with Genroku Legends DLC
primary.why: Muramasa Rebirth is an enhanced Vita port with a new localization and four DLC character scenarios; completeness outweighs Dolphin's potential Wii upscaling.
primary.how_to_play: Play Muramasa Rebirth on PS Vita or PlayStation TV with all four Genroku Legends DLC episodes installed. Use Wii/Dolphin only if you want the original localization and home-console controls.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Wii release; can be upscaled in Dolphin.
all_releases.reason: skip: Dolphin can make the Wii original look cleaner, but it lacks the Vita port's DLC scenarios and new localization.

all_releases.fidelity: Enhanced portable port with DLC story episodes.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete version because Rebirth adds four self-contained DLC stories and a new localization.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Dolphin can upscale the Wii original, but the Vita Rebirth route has exclusive DLC story scenarios, so completeness wins.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Vita DLC must be installed for the complete route; no modern console/PC remaster is documented.
